name: The First Corner
tagline: Teach your robot how to react when a wall blocks its path.
narrative:
The corridor ends at a 90-degree corner.

Your robot already knows how to step forward when the path is clear, but when it encounters a wall, that rule stops matching and the robot stops moving.

Add a new rule to handle walls: when a wall appears ahead, turn right so the robot can face the open path.
objective: Turn the corner, navigate to the goal, and remain there for 3 consecutive ticks.
learningObjective: Combine clear-path movement and wall turning to navigate around obstacles.
intelligenceExplanation:
The starter brain has a rule for walking forward. When it reaches a wall, it stops because no rule matches `wallAhead`.

Place a new wall-handling rule above the forward-stepping rule. Remember: rules are checked from top to bottom, so arrival (`atGoal`) should always come first.
hint: Add WHEN wallAhead -> DO pivot-right above WHEN !wallAhead -> DO step, with WHEN atGoal -> DO hold at the top.
hints: The existing rule only matches when the path ahead is clear.
Add a rule for when a wall is ahead: WHEN wallAhead -> DO pivot-right.
Keep WHEN atGoal -> DO hold at the top so it stops upon reaching the exit.
brief: Extend the straight-line brain to turn at corners and settle on the exit.
context: The corridor turns a corner. The robot knows how to walk forward, but gets stuck when blocked.

steps.label: Add a rule to turn right when a wall is ahead
Reach the goal and stay on it for 3 ticks
steps.hint: Keep WHEN atGoal -> DO hold at the top

rules.description: Move forward when the path is clear.
